A sophisticated and inviting tactile miniature diorama made of warm ivory paper, dark forest-green painted wood, muted terracotta and antique brass, with a small touch of sunny mustard yellow. Soft directional daylight, believable cast shadows, physical craft texture, strong readable silhouette, playful and curious not infantile. Use a dynamic asymmetrical composition that fills most of the landscape without cutting off important objects; ample clear ivory ground, not excessive empty space. Premium museum science-workshop photography mixed with finely crafted layered papercraft. No people, hands, written text, lettering, digits, code, labels, logos or watermarks. No glossy neon sci-fi, no flat corporate vector icons, no UI panels. An ingenious tabletop sorting machine, full of personality: wooden chutes and neatly structured branching tracks guide chunky mineral blocks of visibly different heights into increasing order. Include one beautiful stack tower and a short queue of small green trays, linked by a single unambiguous mechanical path. Restrained brass gears, terracotta pebbles, ivory base. Make the sorting and ordering idea visually immediate. This is conceptual learning art, not a diagram or operating machine.
